changes.old: Verification included trial-identity joins and hashes, reconstruction of the original endpoints, independent implementations of the prediction-transition arithmetic, public-input replay, and visual review of the documents and figures.
changes.new: Verification included exact trial-identifier matching and file checksums, reconstruction of the original endpoints from saved predictions, independent implementations of the prediction-transition arithmetic, reproduction of saved-result calculations from the shared predictions and trial metadata, and visual review of the documents and figures.

changes.old: The five-second cue-anchored windows include the approximately 1.5-second visual cue and subsequent task activity; variable online trial endings can also place feedback or post-task activity within a complete window. Strictly task-anchored windows would address a different phase-specific endpoint. The amplitude rule flagged 1,512 of 7,156 windows (21.1%) and the query sensitivity retained positive mean gains; this check addresses large query amplitudes, while potential artifacts in training/support data remain a separate issue.
changes.new: The five-second cue-anchored windows span the approximately 1.5-second visual cue and subsequent task activity, while variable online trial endings can place feedback or post-task activity within a complete window. Restricting evaluation to strictly task-anchored intervals would therefore address a different, phase-specific endpoint. The amplitude rule flagged 1,512 of 7,156 complete windows (21.1%); the query sensitivity retained positive mean gains after restricting evaluation to unflagged queries. This addresses large query amplitudes, with potential artifacts in training/support data remaining a separate issue.

changes.old: Fourth-order zero-phase filtering defines an offline pipeline. Closed-loop translation requires causal preprocessing and real-time artifact handling. The unweighted source/support union fixes the information available to each update; covariance weighting and signal alignment would require their own controlled comparisons.
changes.new: These comparisons use fourth-order zero-phase filtering for offline analysis, whereas closed-loop translation requires causal preprocessing and real-time artifact handling. Both update methods pooled source/support data without weighting to fix the information available for adaptation; covariance weighting and signal alignment would require their own controlled comparisons.

changes.old: This study uses one 18-participant cohort, with six participants for reliability development and 12 for the primary comparison. Prediction transitions, amplitude sensitivity, influence summaries and sign-flip checks are post-hoc exploratory analyses, and earlier test-result exposure remains part of the study history. EEGNet supplies a frozen source-only reference with 20 additional source-validation labels. Independent multi-session cohorts and prospective support-driven update selection would test how well the component advantage and calibration diagnostics generalize.
changes.new: The findings come from one 18-participant cohort, partitioned into six participants for reliability development and 12 for the primary comparison. The primary endpoint hierarchy and cohort split were predefined; prediction transitions, amplitude sensitivity, participant-influence summaries and exact sign-flip checks were conducted as post-hoc exploratory analyses after observing the original decoding results. EEGNet supplies a frozen source-only reference with 20 additional source-validation labels. Independent multi-session cohorts and prospective support-driven update selection would test how well the component advantage and calibration diagnostics generalize.
